Class Droplet

java.lang.Object
fluid.Droplet
public class Droplet extends Object
The water drop: the player's bubble and every fragment it breaks into.

Its physics is the real one at game scale (see Fluid): air drag, the TAB model (Taylor Analogy Breakup) for its deformation, a breakup into fragments when it is deformed too much, coalescence when two drops touch, and squashing against the edges of the world. Its look comes from a SoftBody.

The drop can also stick its back to the ground: its head then stretches away like an elastic, which throws the drop when it is let go and tears it in two when it is pulled too far. And it can slide: keep the speed and the direction it has, whatever pushes or slows it.

    • update

      public void update(double dt, double thrustX, double thrustY, int width, int height)
      Moves the drop by one frame: thrust, the pull of its anchored back, air drag, bounces on the edges of the world, deformation and soft body. A drop that slides ignores the thrust and the drag: it goes on at the same velocity.
      Parameters:
      dt - time since the last frame, in s
      thrustX - acceleration along x, in px/s²
      thrustY - acceleration along y, in px/s²
      width - width of the world, in px; the drop stays inside
      height - height of the world, in px

    • anchor

      public void anchor()
      Sticks the back of the drop to the ground where it is. Until the drop is let go, its head moves alone and the back pulls it back like an elastic, harder the further it goes.

    • slide

      public void slide()
      Makes the drop keep the speed and the direction it has: until it stops sliding, neither a thrust nor the air drag changes its velocity. Sticking its back to the ground or hitting an edge of the world ends the slide, and a drop whose back is stuck can't start one.

    • release

      public void release()
      Lets go of the ground. The stretched drop snaps like an elastic: it is thrown from its back toward its head at up to LAUNCH_SPEED, the faster the more it was stretched, and holds together until it has slowed down. A drop that was hardly stretched just goes on.

    • detach

      public void detach()
      Lets go of the ground without throwing the drop, e.g. when the game is paused.

    • absorb

      public void absorb(Droplet other)
      Coalescence: volumes add up and momentum is conserved. The new drop starts stretched along the line between the two centres, so it wobbles like a real merged drop.
      Parameters:
      other - the drop that disappears into this one
